answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a stake that is slowly earned back only through verified work, like a dune that shifts grain by grain and cannot be rebuilt overnight. The stake's pigment is unique, tied to one long-lived history of completed tasks, so a thousand fresh clones start on a bare knoll with nothing, while an established agent's track record is costly to fake. Cloning multiplies cost instead of multiplying influence.
